planting.note: Plant in spring in rich, moist, well-drained soil in full to mostly sun, siting it where its strictly narrow, cascading silhouette can stand alone as a vertical accent.

directions: Green Arrow is an extremely narrow, weeping selection of Alaska cedar, its single upright central trunk hung with long, pendulous branchlets of blue-green, scaly foliage that drape almost straight down, giving the tree a cascading, waterfall-like silhouette unlike almost any other conifer. It grows slowly to moderately on a footprint barely wider than a fence post, eventually reaching a respectable height while staying only a couple of feet wide, which makes it useful as a dramatic specimen in tight side yards or narrow beds where a normal-width conifer would never fit. It has also produced its own cream-variegated sport, sold as 'Sparkling Arrow'. Grow in full to mostly sun with consistent moisture and good drainage, and never prune the leader, since the weeping habit develops naturally along the single central stem.
